status_vocabulary.Supported: An official or native mechanism exists and the Harness behavior is verified.
status_vocabulary.Mechanism verified: Harness package, adapter, or installer checks pass, but a real host run is not confirmed.
status_vocabulary.Live verified: A real host session or portal operation produced preserved evidence.
status_vocabulary.Partial: Only part of the capability is available or verified.
status_vocabulary.Unsupported: The host explicitly does not provide the required mechanism.
status_vocabulary.Unknown: The capability was not verified or the official documentation does not establish it.

action_gate.audit_scope: workspace-keyed global state / per-session action-gate records

claude-code.notes: By default a matched command returns no permission decision, so the session's permission mode, rules and auto-mode classifier decide. The hooks reference documents that a hook ask forces a prompt even in auto mode (#107). Deterministic tests verify the deferred result for every permission_mode value and the ask JSON of the opt-in HARNESS_ACTION_GATE_POLICY=always-ask. Live evidence (2026-09-15, plugin 0.3.8-beta, auto mode) showed the earlier forced ask prompting the user; the deferred behavior has no preserved live evidence yet.

codex.notes: Current Codex PreToolUse parses permissionDecision=ask but does not support it; Codex reports the hook failure and continues the tool call. Harness therefore uses exit 2 for matched destructive actions rather than relying on ask semantics.

chatgpt-openai-plugin.notes: Public skills-only distribution does not include local lifecycle hooks; local plugin hook semantics remain a separate host capability.

other.notes: A matched action fails closed until that host has a Harness-verified ask-style decision contract.

hooksLifecycle.notes: Codex officially supports plugin-bundled hooks and the local package is mechanism-tested. The plugin intentionally does not declare unsupported PostToolUseFailure; Codex uses documented PostToolUse semantics instead. Harness also provides an explicit user-config compatibility fallback that copies the packaged runtime and merges exact-owned entries into $CODEX_HOME/hooks.json without changing trust/config.toml. Neither path is promoted to live verified until a real host exposes and executes the hooks.
